statement: Speculative decoding composes multiplicatively with KV-cache quantization for long-context decoding, where the decode phase is memory-bound and KV-cache traffic dominates. QuantSpec's arithmetic-intensity/roofline analysis shows decoding has near-constant, sub-ridge-point arithmetic intensity irrespective of batch size for long contexts, so KV-cache quantization (not weight quantization) is the dominant lever; its hierarchical INT4 design lets the draft model use upper-4-bit KV and the target reconstruct INT8 from both halves, achieving up to 2.49x speedup and running 128K contexts where StreamingLLM/SnapKV OOM. The double full-precision buffer (2G) is the key to keeping acceptance high under speculative rollback. This demonstrates a cross-route composition (quantization + speculative) that is more effective than either alone in the long-context memory-bound regime.
